method: Reproduce one published broad Omdia observation while separating platform-level video time concentration from unmeasured per-niche or per-channel market concentration. Supply tested pure arithmetic for scoped, legitimate nonrepresentative video samples, never infer payouts.

published_video_level_observation.population: Omdia analyst YouTube video viewing-time study, described as global; precise coverage/coding unreported

sample_metric_contract.input_unit: one video_id with one comparable nonnegative observed count for a single metric and observation window
sample_metric_contract.hhi_definition: sum of squared video shares within this sample only
sample_metric_contract.gini_definition: relative mean difference of counts within this sample, not an income inequality estimate
sample_metric_contract.zero_sum_handling: no concentration statistic when all counted events sum to zero
sample_metric_contract.privacy: Use only authorized owner aggregates or properly selected public video metrics; no individual viewers tracked
sample_metric_contract.missing_data_handling: Unknown or negative measures reject input; do not coerce to zero
sample_metric_contract.true_all_niche_concentration_requires: A clearly defined and complete/representatively weighted niche frame, same metric, format and observation window

limitations: The Omdia top-video watch-time share does not establish the fraction of top creators, viewer people, subscribers or income.
Omdia's methodology details and denominator are not independently available; the 91/9 split is a rounded published result, not a reproducible category panel.
Omdia reports a platform-level distribution, not the category concentration of gaming, beauty, education or politics.
Public video views and owner-only watch-time are different units and must never be swapped.
Selected search results, top-ranked videos and highly watched channels suffer exposure and survival selection bias.
Do not treat a synthetic test case as a factual video or earnings observation.
